items.reason: Reverse-spec errors and omissions left required collection, selection, viewer, and persistence behavior unstated or wrong, so coverage questions would name the absent handlers and flows.
REQ-072 omitted three decision-critical fields from the relink candidate boundary, so modelling candidate selection would ask what information the user receives.
Five existing screens lacked required displayed elements in their ruled presentation contracts, producing direct boundary-element coverage questions.
The repair use flow omitted bulk and single auto-repair plus exclusion and its missing-to-deleted destination, which source and alternative-flow coverage would ask for.
The ruled layer omitted the root-only tree empty-state display rule, but the defect is visual overlap/layout rather than a connection, flow destination, or mock operation-set difference.
The mock claimed post-creation type change while the live specification and product locked it, so the same operation was stated two ways and the mock operation set differed from the model.
This order made a new design decision for a third work mode; it did not correct a defective pre-existing ruled statement.
The maintenance menu and delete mode were newly designed behavior, not a correction to an already wrong ruled layer.
The in-tab trash popup, multi-select, and empty-trash behavior were a newly chosen surface design using existing core behavior.
This order wired newly designed work-tab context modes by reusing existing services; no prior ruled-layer defect was identified.
REQ-043 invented a persistent detail panel absent from both the source behavior and new CAD, so sources stated the boundary two ways and the model had an operation absent from the mock.
The order removed a superseded legacy implementation after its requirements were withdrawn or migrated; ruled requirements and core semantics were unchanged.
The display-column evolution and its two editing/rendering surfaces were new CAD-driven product design over an existing attribute.
The ruled CAD already required mode hiding and non-overlap; the recorded defect was implementation layout nonconformance plus a new responsive enhancement.
FL-002/FL-004 settled previously open persistence choices and added the chosen work-tab setting; the former text was not recorded as defective.
CAD and BOM were explicitly healthy; the caret alignment defect was confined to XAML padding and content-alignment implementation.

The E-BOM declaration omitted an already specified mock search operation, but the robustness model could source that operation from the specification/mock and none of K1-K3 names the ledger omission itself.
FL-001 was a design decision that confirmed the current grid behavior with no implementation or ruled-layer correction.
VE-004 resolved an open CAD decision while specification and implementation already required nonblank view names.
IMG-011 deliberately chose merge persistence and introduced compensating undo; the old ruled contract was an unresolved design rather than a defect.
TAG-008 resolved previously unspecified in-use tag deletion policy and changed behavior accordingly; the prior implementation was an acknowledged provisional choice.
TAG-009 was a product-concept decision not to expose tag-definition hierarchy and merely documented already conforming behavior.
The specification, E-BOM, and CAD all fixed the default at 70; only two implementation literals deviated.

Requirements and the leading E-BOM invariant required pre-merge preview and notice while the tray CAD and another invariant omitted them, yielding two stated flows and a mock/model element difference.
K-BOM omitted cross-format decode-path consistency, but that numerical image-quality/computation constraint is outside connection, coverage, and mock-operation checks.
CAD and E-BOM already defined all five search conditions; only three conditions were unimplemented.
The privacy/publication cleanup concerned demo data, manufacturing records, Git history, and release handling, with CAD explicitly inapplicable and no ruled product statement defect.
The existing virtualization contract was sound; WorkTab failed to implement it and its M-BOM/control-plan coverage was missing.
E-SCAN-005 lacked bounded persistence and progress-frequency invariants, but batching, notification rate, and caller occupancy are performance constraints not named by K1-K3.
The image-tab consumer contract omitted the saved-home transition, leaving the view-selection handler's initial destination unstated even though producer requirements were sound.
CAD and requirements omitted the user-facing meaning and quality guarantee of a 100% pHash score, a numerical similarity/computation defect not named by structural checks.
The double-click viewer contract was already fixed in CAD and requirements; WorkTab simply failed to transfer the implementation.
CAD, requirements, and BOM omitted how folder rows participate in sorting, but the defect is a sort-order rule explicitly outside the structural classes.
This was an intentional CAD redesign relocating the existing backup/transfer entry while preserving engine behavior.
The tag dialog implementation failed to transfer the already ruled CAD form; the upstream mock was sound.
CAD already specified wrapping; a horizontal StackPanel's measurement behavior disabled the correctly chosen WrapPanel in implementation.
Both affected mocks already specified flex wrapping; the two remaining implementation containers repeated the same measurement defect.
CAD did not define the many-value preview presentation, but the defect concerns visual overflow and summarization rather than a structural object/flow check.
CAD and BOM left three competing selection-lifetime outcomes after filtering, so modelling that action would raise a direct question about the selected-set destination.
The order identifies input-event robustness bugs while treating CAD silence as nondefective and BOM as healthy.
Implementation conformed to the previous mock; this order transferred a newly refined CAD visual revision without changing behavior.
CAD said scroll position must not break but did not define whether pixel offset or visible-content anchor was preserved; that state/layout semantic is not named by K1-K3.
CAD named a nonexistent docked tag-apply operation while its own interaction prose and mock specified immediate row/value actions, producing two sources and a mock/model operation-set difference.
The shared CAD component contract dropped end-of-scroll reachability, a visual layout/extent requirement that no robustness connection or coverage rule would name.
CMP-011 and REG-C5 already fixed alignment, variants, and verb labels; the shared ConfirmDialog implementation lagged those ruled contracts.
The order intentionally changed the T6 restore transition; the old specification and implementation were mutually correct before the new safety policy.
This was a deliberate redefinition of pending semantics with new adjudication UI; the prior ruled model was explicitly self-consistent.
The staged scan/apply model and summary UI were a product design change from an otherwise correctly implemented one-stage specification.
A single DB status model was sound; only cross-tab cache invalidation and refresh wiring were defective.
REQ-100 already specified recovery by a new scan, while the VM incorrectly re-enabled the same stale staging after partial failure.
The candidate result semantics were correct; only the implementation algorithm scaled quadratically and control-plan complexity coverage was absent.
The missing error vocabulary was recorded in M-CORE-001/M-BOM and implementation followed it; no requirements, 20-spec, E-BOM, K-BOM, mock, or ADR defect was established.
CAD and specification failed to distinguish delta missing from total post-apply missing in the rate definition, a numerical aggregation meaning outside K1-K3.
The missing decision results were correct; only the filesystem implementation repeated per-row existence probes and lacked derived performance coverage.
Pending-review prose delegated relink to repair while its revised mock made pending review the relink actor, duplicating one event across two boundaries and differing operation sets.
The event-count meaning was correct; only the SQL execution plan chose the large missing set as the correlated driver.
